messages.subject: renderPlot Parameters Processing Order
parts: For renderPlot, the width and height parameters are processed before expr is. If I made a reactive expression for calculating it, I would need to copy some preliminary table filtering code twice, since when the reactive expression is called for width or height, it can't simply get variables referring to the filtered data table from renderPlot's expression, because the expression is not the parent environment in that case. Could renderPlot evaluate expr first, which would allow users to put the dimensions into the global environment and easily refer to them for width and height, if both of them were processed after expr ? Calling the reactive function twice is also unsuitable, for example, if it pops up a modal dialog message because all the of code was copied into the reactive expression, including the table subsetting code, which depends on at least one table row being selected, otherwise popping up an error message in a modal. If it were inside the reactive expression, it would annoyingly pop up twice to the user.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: renderPlot Parameters Processing Order
parts:
The table filtering code should also be a reactive expression. And also, if a reactive expression is called twice without an intervening change to its reactive dependencies, then the second call will not cause the reactive expression code to be executed, because reactive expressions cache their results.

There's no way expr can execute before width/height. The graphics device must be initialized to the correct width/height before plotting code can execute.
